verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs show event-driven automation. CI/CD pipelines run scans automatically when code is committed or a merge request is created, users configure this in the project's CI/CD configuration file, and pushes are blocked automatically when secrets are detected. However, the evidence covers only security-scan triggers, not a general facility for defining custom event-to-action rules. Missing for 10: documentation of general user-defined rule syntax or conditions, a range of event types beyond commit/MR/push, arbitrary custom actions, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: scans run automatically as part of CI/CD pipelines when code is committed or merge requests are created
Enable SAST in your project by using either the UI or editing your project’s GitLab CI/CD configuration file.
The push is blocked if secrets are detected, unless you skip secret push protection.
For some secret types, GitLab can even automatically revoke the exposed secret.
